title: Neurocognitive Architecture
description: Brain anatomy assets, neural network overlays, and semantic mechanisms for attention, prediction, memory, error-driven learning, pattern completion, and temporal integration — grounded in neuroscientific models without reducing cognition to anatomy.

assets.description: A canonical lateral brain silhouette with labelled cortical lobes (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, cerebellum, brainstem).
A layered node-and-edge graph representing neural populations with adjustable depth, branching and connection density.
A schematic cortical column with layered input, processing and output zones and vertical integration paths.
A graded spatial field with a high-resolution center fading into peripheral suppression — can be positioned anywhere in frame.
A forward-propagating wave or arrow that travels from a source toward a target, with optional intensity envelope.
A fading or consolidating path that can be reinforced, decayed, or overwritten over time.
provenance: memory_before_brains_platinum.py: trace as condition of access

assets.description: A salient mismatch marker — a flash, spike or discordant oscillation — that appears where prediction and input diverge.
provenance: cells_that_solve_problems_platinum.py: problem signals as error-guided correction

assets.description: A rhythmic waveform trace (theta, alpha, beta, gamma) with adjustable frequency, amplitude and phase — can be shown as Lissajous figures or line traces.
provenance: breath_clock_brain_platinum.py: embodied time and cortical rhythms

mechanisms.description: A wide field of equipotential items is narrowed by a moving aperture that selects one region while suppressing others, demonstrating that attention is selective enhancement, not merely revealing what was already there.
mechanisms.motionProof: Items outside the aperture change opacity or relevance as the aperture moves, proving that selection actively modifies access rather than passively illuminating pre-existing content.
provenance: attention_creates_finite_self_platinum.py: selective awareness constructs a finite self

mechanisms.description: A top-down prediction signal meets a bottom-up sensory signal; their convergence produces an updated prediction, while their divergence produces a salient error signal that drives revision.
mechanisms.motionProof: The prediction and input remain visibly separate until convergence, and the error marker appears only where they fail to align — proving the temporal process of predictive inference rather than a static label.
provenance: cells_that_solve_problems_platinum.py: problem solving as error correction

mechanisms.description: A partial or degraded input pattern progressively reconstructs into a complete stored template through spreading activation across a network.
mechanisms.motionProof: The reconstruction proceeds from fragment to whole along associative paths, proving that completion is an active process of spreading activation — not a lookup of a pre-stored image.
provenance: memory_before_brains_platinum.py: memory is reconstruction, not storage

mechanisms.description: Multiple parallel traces reorganise over time: some stabilise and strengthen, others decay and are pruned, producing a consolidated network that differs from the initial encoding.
mechanisms.motionProof: The trace set changes visibly from a dense simultaneous pattern to a sparser structured one — proving consolidation as reorganisation rather than mere preservation.

mechanisms.description: A local activation event produces timed waves of activity that spread through a network along weighted connections, with amplitude diminishing or amplifying at each junction.
mechanisms.motionProof: The activation reaches different nodes at different times with different magnitudes — performing propagation rather than merely illuminating a static graph.
provenance: cells_solving_problem_platinum.py: signal propagation through cellular networks

mechanisms.description: Several candidate features or interpretations compete for a unified binding; one stabilises as the dominant percept while alternatives remain present as suppressed traces.
mechanisms.motionProof: Multiple candidates remain active until one visibly suppresses the others, proving binding as a competitive temporal process rather than a one-shot assignment.
provenance: consciousness_container_platinum.py: unified field from competing contents

mechanisms.description: Sequentially presented items leave persistent traces that accumulate into a single episodic representation, with earlier items fading but remaining structurally present.
mechanisms.motionProof: Earlier items visibly persist in modified form as later items arrive, proving that temporal integration is cumulative retention — not replacement of one frame by the next.
provenance: time_is_produced_by_forgetting_platinum.py: sequence produced by retention and loss

mechanisms.description: A prediction error signal propagates backward through a network, modifying connection weights so that subsequent predictions more closely match the input.
mechanisms.motionProof: The weight of each connection changes measurably following the error signal, and the subsequent prediction differs from the first — proving learning as weight modification driven by error, not mere exposure.

selectionPolicy.captionPolicy: Use neuroanatomical labels only to disambiguate structures; narration carries the cognitive or phenomenological prose.
forbiddenLiteralizations: glowing neuron icon with no encoded relation
static brain region colouring without temporal process
selectionPolicy.epistemicRule: Mark computational models, biomedical schematics, phenomenological reports and functional models separately. Never imply that a computational diagram proves a phenomenological claim or vice versa.
